description: In this seminar, students will be introduced to the interdisciplinary field of energy humanities, which seeks to understand the relationship between culture and the energy sources that people produce and consume. Students will encounter foundational texts in the field, alongside literature, film, and visual media that explore how both fossil fuels and renewable energy influence aspects of life ranging from everyday decisions to local ecosystems to global politics. The course will devote significant attention to environmental justice issues related to energy extraction and the renewable energy transition. This is an upper-division course in which students will take a leading role in discussions. Students will also produce a substantial research-based project with ample opportunity to pursue their personal interests within the broader course topic.
name: Top: Global Energy Humanities
title: Advanced Research Topics in Environmental Studies
